summary: Lincoln National Forest tower moved from the 1935 Mayhill CCC-era site to James Ridge in 1967; volunteer-staffed as of 2020 and open to visitors.

facts.design: 62-foot steel tower with a 7-by-7-foot steel cab; the register calls the tower an Aermotor LX-24 type that has been remodeled

access.note: Forest Service lists the site as open; no potable water; restroom information not available. Check current forest alerts before visiting.

events.note: Built as the Mayhill Lookout (LX-24 cab on a 48-foot tower) at the Mayhill CCC camp
Moved from Mayhill and re-erected at James Ridge

Registered with the National Historic Lookout Register on August 30, 2015

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1935 build date belongs to the Mayhill lookout; the register gives no build year for the James Ridge site, so 1967 is the date the present site was occupied.

notes_for_editor: The 48-foot Mayhill figure (Forest Service Mayhill page) and the 62-foot James Ridge figure (register and Forest Service James Ridge page) are both printed and unexplained; not reconciled. height_m left unset because 62 feet is overall tower height, not cab-floor height. The Forest Service calls LX-24 the cab style while the register calls the tower an LX-24 type; the story uses the register's design wording. NRHP addendum status is as of the 2020 chapter report only; check the NPS record before publication. Staffing is from the 2020 report; current staffing is unknown. The Forest Service page was last updated February 19, 2025. The recreation.gov listing (RIDB 240834 in the record) was not read.
